A1.justification: Both PDFs describe InfoTok and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. All material supports reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered tables.

before.justification: V1 reports original video-reconstruction experiments on TokenBench and DAVIS, router and compressor ablations, and resolution and inference-latency results in Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 reports original TokenBench and DAVIS reconstruction results, ablations in Section 4.3, and resolution and latency experiments in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The ELBO-based router, likelihood-guided token selection, transformer compressor/decompressor, InfoTok-Flex variant, reconstruction objective, and inference procedure remain unchanged in Sections 2–3 and Appendix B.

E1.justification: The stated training data and video-reconstruction coverage are unchanged. Both evaluate TokenBench and DAVIS and retain the additional resolution/aspect-ratio scenarios in Appendix C.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Open-MAGVIT2-UCF, OmniTokenizer, Cosmos-DV4x8x8, and ElasticTok. The optimal-router, R2L/Jump masking, architecture, and latency comparisons also retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix B retain the same preprocessing, dataset splits and sample counts, 33-frame clip procedure, metrics, model configurations, and training budgets. Appendix C testing protocols also match.

E4.justification: Both contain the same router-versus-optimal, token-masking, cross-architecture, compression-rate, and resolution analyses. V1 Tables 3–4 become the two panels of v2 Table 3 without changing the analyses or evidence.

E5.justification: Both report point estimates without seed/repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2 introduces no statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Matched tables, plotted curves, and reconstruction examples retain their results. For example, Table 1 reports InfoTok-Flex at BPP16 = 0.56 with TokenBench PSNR 29.30 and FVD 71 in both versions. Appendix C resolution and latency values also match.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, Theorems 2.1, 2.2, and 3.1, and proofs in Appendix A are unchanged. Pagination and cross-reference formatting do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: Both retain the claims about inefficient fixed/data-agnostic tokenization, near-optimal ELBO-based allocation, and improved token efficiency. The abstract's 20% token-saving and 2.3× compression claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of routing effectiveness and compression-quality tradeoffs remain unchanged. Section 6 retains the same modality-generalization discussion and limitations concerning the extra decoder pass and absent downstream evaluation.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-page link and replaces the first-page 'Code available soon' statement with 'Code here' linked to a repository. Appendix B technical details and the supplementary-code statement remain unchanged. The PDFs establish improved access information, but do not verify repository contents.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning against earlier tokenization methods remain unchanged. Added bibliography links back to citing pages are navigation changes, not additions to related work.

P1.justification: V2 updates the publication header and one author affiliation, lightly edits the compressor-ablation prose, and polishes Appendix D's language-model-use statement. The section order and scientific narrative remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 merges v1 Tables 3–4 into a side-by-side Table 3, relocates Table 2, and renumbers subsequent tables. Several figures use higher-resolution images; hyperlink styling, bibliography backreferences, and page flow also change.

improvement.justification: Sharper reconstruction figures make visual comparisons easier to inspect, while direct project/code links and bibliography backreferences improve resource discovery and navigation. The consolidated ablation layout adds modest presentation benefits. Methods, proofs, experimental evidence, and stated limitations remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
